bench.note: Flat or floor press. The floor limits shoulder extension; dumbbells require more independent shoulder control.

incline.note: An incline biases the clavicular (upper) chest. Shoulder contribution increases as the bench gets steeper.

decline.note: Lower chest emphasis; the whole pectoralis major still contributes.

machine_press.note: The machine or Smith track guides the load, reducing balance demands compared with free weights.

machine_incline.note: Inclined, supported machine press; upper chest emphasis.

close_press.note: Triceps emphasis. A JM press blends pressing and elbow extension; its chest contribution is smaller.

pushup.note: The trunk stays braced as the arms press. Serratus anterior moves and controls the shoulder blades.

dip.note: More forward torso lean generally increases chest contribution. Assistance reduces the load, not the basic muscle pattern.

fly.note: Biceps help hold the elbow angle; they are not the main mover. A floor fly limits the bottom range.

cable_fly.note: Standing cable fly or press-around. Torso bracing resists the cable's pull; cable height changes chest emphasis.

pec_deck.note: Chest fly with the torso supported. Handle and elbow-pad designs have different stabilization demands.

pullover.note: Shoulder extension involves both lats and chest. Rib position, elbow angle and range affect emphasis.

row.note: Unsupported bent-over row: spinal extensors and abdominal bracing hold the torso still.

one_arm_row.note: Single-arm row. Obliques resist torso rotation; hand or bench support reduces lower-back demand.

supported_row.note: Chest support reduces the need to hold a bent-over torso position.

seated_row.note: Seated row without chest support. Keep the torso steady instead of rocking with the load.

one_arm_cable_row.note: Single-arm cable row: the trunk resists the cable's rotational pull.

high_row.note: Assumes a supported high-row machine. Elbow path changes the balance between lats and upper back.

inverted_row.note: Bodyweight row; core and glutes hold the body in a straight line.

pulldown.note: Vertical pull. Grip and elbow path change emphasis; forearm flexors maintain the grip.

one_arm_pulldown.note: Single-arm pulldown; obliques help resist leaning and rotation.

pullup.note: Overhand pull-up. Assisted versions reduce load while preserving the basic pulling pattern.

chinup.note: Underhand grip gives the biceps a stronger role than in a typical overhand pull-up.

straight_arm_pull.note: Shoulder extension with a nearly fixed elbow angle. Triceps assist shoulder extension and hold the elbow position.

overhead_press.note: Standing strict press. The clean-and-press has an additional lower-body pull phase; see its separate option below.

seated_press.note: Seated press; back support reduces torso demands. Arnold presses add rotation. Behind-the-neck variations require suitable shoulder mobility.

machine_shoulder_press.note: Guided overhead press. A supported torso and guided path reduce balance demands.

lateral_raise.note: Raise out to the side. The supraspinatus (part of the rotator cuff) also assists the lift while stabilizing the shoulder.

seated_raise.note: Seated lateral raise; sitting reduces whole-body balance demands.

fdl_raise.note: FDL is interpreted as a front / lateral / rear-delt raise sequence. Each phase emphasizes a different deltoid head.

rear_fly.note: Rear-delt fly. Bent-over versions need spinal support; standing cable versions need torso bracing.

reverse_deck.note: Supported reverse fly; shoulder blades retract as the arms open.

face_pull.note: Assumes a face pull ending with external shoulder rotation. External rotators both move and stabilize the shoulder.

pull_apart.note: Warm-up activation, rather than a heavy working set.

external_rotation.note: Infraspinatus and teres minor externally rotate the shoulder. The cuff is shown schematically.

internal_rotation.note: Subscapularis is the principal cuff internal rotator; assistance depends on arm position.

shrug.note: Upper trapezius elevates the shoulder blades. Levator scapulae also assists but is not separately drawn.

seated_shrug.note: Seated shrug; the seat reduces postural demands.

curl.note: Supinated elbow curl. Forearm muscles stabilize the wrist; the torso stays still.

supported_curl.note: Seated, incline or upper-arm-supported curl. Shoulder position changes the biceps' working length.

hammer_curl.note: Neutral grip emphasizes brachialis and brachioradialis. Forearm flexors and extensors hold the wrist position.

zottman.note: Supinated lifting phase and pronated lowering phase involve the biceps, brachialis and brachioradialis.

wrist_curl.note: Forearm supported; wrist flexion targets the wrist and finger flexor group.

reverse_wrist.note: Forearm supported; wrist extension targets the forearm extensor group.

pushdown.note: Cable elbow extension with the upper arms held still. Rope Extension is interpreted as a rope pushdown.

overhead_extension.note: Overhead elbow extension lengthens the triceps long head. Seated or supported versions reduce torso demand.

skullcrusher.note: Lying elbow extension; shoulder muscles hold the upper arms in position.

machine_triceps.note: Supported elbow-extension machine; upper-arm support reduces shoulder and torso demands.

kickback.note: Assumes a bent-over dumbbell kickback. Bench support reduces spinal stabilization demand.

squat.note: Knee and hip extension. A plie stance increases adductor involvement; depth and stance alter emphasis.

front_squat.note: Anterior loading increases the demand to keep the torso upright.

machine_squat.note: Guided squat. Hack and pendulum pads support the torso; a Smith squat still requires active trunk bracing.

sissy_squat.note: Knee-dominant squat with extended hips. Hand support reduces balance requirements.

leg_press.note: The back pad supports the torso. Foot placement and depth affect hip and knee contributions.

lunge.note: Split-stance or stepping leg exercise. Hip abductors help keep the pelvis level; both sides are shown for alternating sets.

lateral_lunge.note: Sideways lunge; adductors lengthen and contribute to returning to the starting position.

smith_lunge.note: Guided reverse lunge reduces free-weight balance demands.

stepup.note: Step-up on the working leg. Hip abductors stabilize the pelvis.

deadlift.note: Conventional floor pull. Spinal extensors brace rather than deliberately flexing and extending the back. Snatch grip increases upper-back demand.

rack_pull.note: Raised starting position reduces range and usually reduces knee-extension demand relative to a floor deadlift.

rdl.note: Hip hinge with relatively little knee movement. Spinal extensors hold the back position.

single_rdl.note: Single-leg hinge adds pelvic and balance control; both sides are shown for alternating sets.

good_morning.note: Hip hinge with the load supported at the shoulders.

hip_thrust.note: Hip extension with the upper back supported. Keep the trunk and pelvis controlled.

back_extension.note: A hip-dominant extension emphasizes glutes and hamstrings; controlled spinal extension increases erector involvement. This map shows both common techniques.

reverse_hyper.note: Legs move while the torso is supported.

superman.note: Prone trunk and hip extension with arms raised; keep the range controlled.

leg_curl.note: Knee flexion. Gastrocnemius can assist; seated and lying variants change hamstring length.

standing_leg_curl.note: Single-leg knee flexion with the torso upright. The stance hip and core stabilize the pelvis.

glute_ham.note: Knee flexion with hip extension and trunk control.

leg_extension.note: Supported knee extension isolates the quadriceps.

abduction.note: Gluteus medius and minimus abduct the hip; tensor fasciae latae also assists but is not separately drawn.

adduction.note: The inner-thigh adductor group draws the thighs together.

standing_calf.note: Straight-knee calf raise emphasizes gastrocnemius with soleus contributing. Unspecified calf exercises assume a standing, straight-knee version.

supported_calf.note: Straight-knee calf press or guided raise. The equipment reduces balance demands compared with an unsupported standing raise.

seated_calf.note: Bent knees shorten the gastrocnemius, shifting emphasis toward soleus.

crunch.note: Trunk flexion. Cable and machine versions add resistance; keep the hips relatively still.

situp.note: A full sit-up involves both trunk flexion and hip flexion.

leg_raise.note: Hip flexors raise the thighs. Abs resist the tendency for the lower back to arch; adding a pelvic curl gives the abs a moving role.

reverse_crunch.note: Abs curl the pelvis toward the ribs. Hip flexors help hold the legs in position rather than swinging them.

v_up.note: Combined trunk and hip flexion brings the torso and legs together.

hanging_raise.note: Abs posteriorly tilt the pelvis; hip flexors raise the thighs. Grip and shoulder muscles support the hang.

bicycle.note: Trunk flexion and rotation with alternating hip flexion.

plank.note: The target muscles work isometrically to resist spinal extension; targets need not move a joint.

side_plank.note: Lateral core stability. Quadratus lumborum also contributes but is not separately drawn; both sides are shown for alternating holds.

hollow.note: Isometric anti-extension hold; maintain a controlled pelvic position.

rollout.note: Anti-extension core work as the arms reach overhead.

jump_squat.note: Explosive squat and jump; the same muscle groups control the landing.

deep_squat.note: Warm-up squat through a comfortable range.

pass_through.note: Shoulder mobility: highlighted target regions are moved or lengthened, not necessarily strengthened. Use a wide, comfortable grip.

child_cobra.note: Alternating positions lengthen different trunk regions. These are mobility targets, not simultaneous prime movers.

child_reach.note: Reach forward or sideways to lengthen the back and side of the trunk.

leg_swing.note: Dynamic hip mobility. Front-to-back and side-to-side swings move different regions; the stance leg stabilizes the pelvis.

lunge_arch.note: Mobility targets the front of the hip and trunk; avoid forcing lumbar extension.

side_lunge_stretch.note: Inner-thigh stretch; the bent leg supports the position.

hamstring_stretch.note: Lengthen the hamstrings with a controlled hip hinge; hand support reduces balance demand.

world_stretch.note: Multi-position lunge and rotation sequence. Highlights show regions mobilized across the sequence, rather than simultaneous contraction.

foam_roll.note: Shown regions are possible soft-tissue targets, not working muscles. The program does not prescribe a specific rolling area or position.

clean.note: Clean phase: hip and knee extension accelerate the bar, then the shoulders support the front-rack catch. The press phase has a different map.
